assessment: The stipulated baseline meets the time target in 20 of 30 sessions. Unexpected caption versions and one unexpected video cut are observed; their causes remain unresolved. Completion order, input pairing and time spent locating previews merit separate measurement. Existing processing usage does not establish festival capacity.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each render to an immutable record of its caption and video hashes, and present that identity alongside the editor-selected intended pair. An earlier request finishing later must not change which pair is marked intended.
openings.delta: Replace completion sequence as the apparent version identity with a persistent input-pair identity. Workers read the recorded snapshots; previews expose the corresponding caption wording and video identity. Preserve the last delivered pair and original wording as an accessible retained record.
openings.prediction: With deliberately reversed completion order, editors still select the intended pair, and every delivered preview matches its recorded input hashes. This need not reduce render duration.
openings.probe: Use fabricated footage in private staging to interleave caption and video changes and force reverse completion. Have both editors identify intended and last-delivered versions without a worksheet; verify the worker inputs against each record. Scope implementation within four engineer-days and one editor-day.
assumptions: Immutable input snapshots and worker binding are feasible within the stated budget.
Recorded hashes are checked against actual worker inputs, not merely attached as labels.

openings.claim: Does the slow-session tail predominantly occur before the intended preview becomes available or after it is already available?
openings.delta: Distinguishes a rendering or scheduling intervention from an identification or review intervention before spending the remaining engineering allowance.
openings.prediction: A waiting-dominated explanation predicts that intended previews become available after minute 15 in most late sessions. A selection/review explanation predicts availability before minute 15 followed by delayed correct identification.
openings.probe: Pair timestamped request, start and completion events with editor-observed final-edit and correct-identification times in staged workflows. In 30 new sessions, record both intervals and unintended-pair deliveries; assess the stated 90% target rather than assuming either explanation.
assumptions: The intended pair and final edit can be identified reliably.
Editor observation fits within one editor-day shared with A1; otherwise sampling must be limited and conclusions remain provisional.
